comments.author: GdoongMathew
comments.body:
Hi @aditya0by0, thanks for reporting this issue. 

I don’t have extensive experience with `LightningDataModule`, but from what I can tell, the intention of `load_from_checkpoint` does not seem to be to instantiate any subclasses via the base `LightningDataModule` class. This behavior is consistent with how `LightningModule` works as well.

For instance,
```python
>>> class BoringModule(LightningModule):
...    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
...        ...

>>> BoringModule.load_from_checkpoint(ckpt_path)  # this should work as expected
>>> LightningModule.load_from_checkpoint(ckpt_path)  # this won't work
```

Regarding `cls_spec.varkw` is False, this happens because the inspected `cls_spec` corresponds to `LightningDataModule` rather than the user's custom subclass. If we change same line in 
https://github.com/Lightning-AI/pytorch-lightning/pull/21478/changes#diff-66f006dbadabdd4826bf8fb6dcb776fe4b73871f73daf05f205b6e27aae7a548R1102 to `TestDataSaveHparams.load_from_checkpoint(checkpoint_path)`, then the newly added test cases should pass.

comments.author: aditya0by0
comments.body:
@GdoongMathew , thanks for the detailed response and for taking a look at this.

> This behavior is consistent with how `LightningModule` works as well.

I don’t think this is fully consistent with `LightningModule`. To illustrate this, there is an existing test case that explicitly relies on this behavior:

[https://github.com/Lightning-AI/pytorch-lightning/blob/master/tests/tests_pytorch/test_cli.py#L1069-L1070](https://github.com/Lightning-AI/pytorch-lightning/blob/master/tests/tests_pytorch/test_cli.py#L1069-L1070)

In this test, calling `LightningModule.load_from_checkpoint(...)` correctly instantiates the concrete subclass specified via `_class_path`, even though the base `LightningModule` class is used to invoke `load_from_checkpoint`.

There is also some related discussion here that touches on the same expectation:
[https://github.com/Lightning-AI/pytorch-lightning/discussions/21474](https://github.com/Lightning-AI/pytorch-lightning/discussions/21474)

Coming back to the initially provided reproducible example, if we add the following lines:

```python
model = LightningModule.load_from_checkpoint(checkpoint_path)
assert isinstance(model, TestModelSaveHparams)
```

the assertion passes as expected, which further demonstrates that `LightningModule.load_from_checkpoint` *does* restore the subclass when `_class_path` is present.

This is why the behavior of `LightningDataModule.load_from_checkpoint` felt inconsistent to me, and why I believe the current behavior is a bug rather than an intentional design difference.

Happy to clarify further or adjust the approach if I’m missing something.

comments.author: GdoongMathew
aditya0by0
comments.body:
@GdoongMathew, thanks for the reply.

You’re absolutely right that this is a CLI-specific use case, and that `_instantiator` and `_class_path` are only stored in the checkpoint when using `LightningCLI`. That said, this behavior is still quite valuable in practice: when all model and datamodule classes are already available in the environment, it allows dynamic loading and instantiation at runtime from checkpoint without requiring the user to explicitly reference the concrete class. 

This is especially useful for reproducibility and quick experiment workflows built around the CLI for my use case.

Regarding adding `*args, **kwargs` to `LightningDataModule.__init__`, I don’t think this would introduce issues. `LightningDataModule` and `LightningModule` already share a very similar inheritance structure and both include `HyperparametersMixin` and `DataHooks`:

```python
class LightningDataModule(DataHooks, HyperparametersMixin):
    ...
```

```python
class LightningModule(
    _DeviceDtypeModuleMixin,
    HyperparametersMixin,
    ModelHooks,
    DataHooks,
    CheckpointHooks,
    Module,
):
    ...
```
>I also wouldn’t be opposed to adding *args, **kwargs to LightningDataModule.__init__. If that’s the direction we want to take, I’d be happy to help with the review.

Given this similarity, aligning `LightningDataModule` with `LightningModule` by allowing `*args, **kwargs` in the constructor seems consistent. Hence, I’m happy to proceed with this direction and would appreciate your review on the PR.
